questions.question: The Koya movement in Malkangiri, during 1880, (now in Odisha) was led by:
questions.solution:
• Koya Movement: Tama Dora
  • Detail: A tribal movement against the British in the Odisha/Andhra border region.

questions.question: The headquarters of the Ghadar Movement was located at which of the following places?
questions.solution:
• Ghadar Headquarters: San Francisco
  • Fact: The headquarters was known as 'Yugantar Ashram'.

questions.question: Which of the following ancient texts is a source to study Bharatanatyam?
questions.solution:
• Abhinaya Darpana: Abhinaya Darpana
  • Arts: A primary technical text for Bharatanatyam dance.

questions.question: What did the term ‘bhoga’ refer to during the medieval period?
questions.solution:
• Bhoga (Medieval): Revenue assignments
  • Term: Referred to the right of the king or assigned lord to enjoy specific produce.

questions.question: Who among the following organised Sarvajanik Ganesh Utsav to inculcate national sentiments among the masses?
questions.solution:
• Ganesh Utsav: Lokmanya Tilak
  • Purpose: To create a sense of unity and bypass bans on political meetings.

questions.question: Alvars were the devotees of which South Indian cult?
questions.solution:
• Alvars: Vaishnavism
  • Bhakti: Tamil poet-saints who were devotees of Lord Vishnu.

questions.question: Who among the following Mughals built Moti Masjid in the Agra Fort complex?
questions.solution:
• Moti Masjid (Agra): Shah Jahan
  • Fact: Built entirely of white marble inside the Agra Fort.

questions.question: Who is referred to as “Frontier Gandhi”?
questions.solution:
• Frontier Gandhi: Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan
  • Leadership: Leader of the non-violent 'Khudai Khidmatgar' movement.

questions.question: In which year was the Vernacular Press Act passed?
questions.solution:
• Vernacular Press Act: 1878
  • Viceroy: Lord Lytton.

questions.question: Who among the following was a member of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.solution:
• Drafting Committee Member: Dr. KM Munshi
  • Constitution: He was one of the key figures in framing the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: In which year did Swami Dayanand Saraswati establish Arya Samaj?
questions.solution:
• Arya Samaj Year: 1875
  • Founder: Swami Dayanand Saraswati.

questions.question: The lofty gates erected in the courtyard of the temples in south India were called ________.
questions.solution:
• Gopuram: gopuram
  • Architecture: The monumental entrance towers of South Indian temples.

questions.question: ‘Uttar Ramcharita’ was the composition of which of the following poets?
questions.solution:
• Uttar Ramcharita: Bhavabhuti
  • Literature: An 8th-century Sanskrit play about the later life of Rama.

questions.question: 'Ghiyasuddin Balban introduced the customs of *Sijda’ and ‘Paibos’ as normal forms of salutations to the king as a part of __________ etiquette.
questions.solution:
• Sijda & Paibos: Court
  • Purpose: Balban introduced these to assert the divine status of the Sultan.

questions.question: Who founded the East India Association in London?
questions.solution:
• East India Association: Dadabhai Naoroji
  • Fact: Established in London to discuss Indian grievances with the British public.

questions.question: Which of the following associations was formed in Maharashtra to get social justice for the weaker sections of society?
questions.solution:
• Satya Shodhak Samaj: Satya Shodhak Samaj
  • Founder: Jyotirao Phule in Maharashtra.

questions.question: Which of the following cities was built by Humayun at Delhi?
questions.solution:
• Dinpanah: Dinpanah
  • History: The 'Asylum of Faith', a city founded by Humayun at Delhi.

questions.question: The name of the Brahmin priest who later came to be known as Ramakrishna Paramahansa is:
questions.solution:
• Ramakrishna Paramahansa: Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya
  • Fact: He was the spiritual guru of Swami Vivekananda.

questions.question: In which language was the work of Raja Ram Mohan Roy, ‘Gift to Monotheists’ originally written?
questions.solution:
• Gift to Monotheists: Persian
  • Original Name: Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin.

questions.question: In which century did the Arab traveler Sulaiman visit India?
questions.solution:
• Arab Traveler: 9th
  • Detail: Sulaiman visited the Palas and Rashtrakutas during the 9th century.

questions.question: Which great leader died due to his injuries in the Anti-Simon Commission Protest of 1928?
questions.solution:
• Simon Commission Protest: Lala Lajpat Rai
  • 1928: He succumbed to injuries sustained during a lathi charge.

questions.question: Who was the first to mention the incident of Jauhar in Persian?
questions.solution:
• First Persian Jauhar Mention: Amir Khusrau
  • Incident: He witnessed and recorded the Jauhar at Ranthambore in 1301.

questions.question: Who composed 'Shahnama'?
questions.solution:
• Shahnama: Ferdowsi
  • Literature: The national epic of the Persian-speaking world.

questions.question: The Muhammedan Literary Society founded in Calcutta in 1863 was founded by:
questions.solution:
• Muhammedan Literary Society: Nawab Abdul Latif
  • Context: A pioneering modern education movement for Muslims in Bengal.

questions.question: Rast-Goftar, a newspaper, propagated the messages of socio-religious reforms for which of the following societies?
questions.solution:
• Rast-Goftar: Parsi
  • Detail: It means 'The Truth Teller' and was started by Dadabhai Naoroji.
